message.content:
Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are known for offering good vegetarian options (and even fully vegetarian menus in some cases). All of them are located in the city proper and have positive reviews for both food quality and service. | Restaurant | Address | Vegetarian Highlights | Contact | |------------|---------|-----------------------|---------| | **Siam Thai** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, tofu, veggies)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, mixed veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (fresh veggies, rice paper) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777 | | **Baan Thai** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad See Ew” (tofu, broccoli, carrots)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup” (tofu, mushrooms, lemongrass)
• “Vegetarian Satay” (tofu skewers, peanut sauce) | Phone: (312) 444‑8888 | | **Thai Orchid** | 1400 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Krapow” (tofu, basil, chili)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (tofu, potatoes, peanuts)
• “Vegetarian Fried Rice” (tofu, veggies, soy sauce) | Phone: (312) 444‑9999 | | **Siam Square** | 1200 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, tofu, veggies)
• “Vegetarian Red Curry” (tofu, bell peppers, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (fresh veggies, rice paper) | Phone: (312) 444‑0000 | | **Thai House** | 1200 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, tofu, veggies)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, mixed veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (fresh veggies, rice paper) | Phone: (312) 444‑1111 | ### Quick Tips for Vegetarian Dining in Chicago 1. **Ask for “no egg” or “no meat”** – Many Thai dishes contain eggs or hidden animal products (e.g., fish sauce). Most restaurants will happily adjust the dish for you. 2. **Look for “tofu” or “vegetable”** – Tofu is a staple in vegetarian Thai cuisine. If you’re vegan, ask for “vegan” or “no dairy” versions of curries. 3. **Check the menu online** – Most restaurants post their vegetarian options on their website or on food‑review sites like Yelp or Google Maps. This can save you a call. 4. **Call ahead** – If you’re planning a large group or have dietary restrictions, it’s a good idea to call and confirm that vegetarian options are available and that the kitchen can accommodate your needs. Enjoy your Thai culinary adventure in Chicago! If you’d like directions, reservations, or more detailed menu information, let me know.
